Subject: DPA snippets + subprocessor phrasing for public site

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, attaching the current DPA draft and a rough set of short bullets we think could sit on the hosted API product pages (sales/console facing). Two asks from Acme that I want to loop you in on:

1) Can we provide a single-line "what we do with data" blurb that is customer-facing and easy for procurement to scan?
2) They asked for a short, plain-language explanation of subprocessors and cross-border transfers (one or two sentences) rather than the long legal list.

Laura and Kim — could you take a pass on two versions: (A) a one-line summary for the product card, and (B) a 2–3 sentence layperson paragraph we can include in the DPA FAQ? I put the working files in the attachment: public-snippet-proposals.docx and dpa-draft-v3.pdf.

Target: send back by EOD tomorrow so I can share with Acme Legal before their procurement review on Monday.

Thanks —
Evelyn

Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0157

Attachments: dpa-draft-v3.pdf (PDF, 230kb), public-snippet-proposals.docx (Docx, 18kb)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA snippets + subprocessor phrasing for public site

Evelyn —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the draft and sketched two candidate texts below. I kept the tone short and procurement-friendly. Highlighting things I intentionally avoided putting on product pages: enumerating every subprocessor and detailed transfer mechanisms (we can link to the full subprocessor map).

Candidate A (one-line product card):
"Redwood processes customer request data to generate model outputs; we do not train on customer data and restrict access with audit logs and contractual controls."

Candidate B (FAQ paragraph, 2–3 sentences):
"We engage trusted subprocessors (cloud and security providers) to operate our service. We limit subprocessors' access to only what they need to run the service, maintain contractual safeguards (e.g., data processing terms, SOC 2 controls), and publish a current subprocessor list. For customers with EU data residency or specific controls, we offer private deployment and contractual transfer protections."

A few editorial notes:
- Swap "request data" for "API request data" if that reads cleaner for product pages.
- Rishi, is the reference to "SOC 2" OK here or should we say "industry-standard controls"?

Happy to iterate —
Laura

Laura Bennett
Director, Developer Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T12:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA snippets + subprocessor phrasing for public site

Laura / Evelyn —

Quick note: "SOC 2" as a phrase is fine for buyer-facing marketing when paired with an invitation to request evidence under NDA. For the public DPA/terms copy I'd prefer "industry-standard technical and organizational controls" to avoid implying full audit availability on the website. So tweak Candidate B last sentence to: "...maintain contractual safeguards and industry-standard technical and organizational controls; we also publish a current subprocessor list."

Also, for the one-line card, swap to "API request data" and replace "do not train on" with "we do not use customer API request data to train our public models" — slightly more explicit.

Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal (Commercial)
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: OliveTech Legal <legal@olivetech.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA snippets + subprocessor phrasing for public site

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from Acme Legal:

1) When you say "we publish a current subprocessor list", where is that list hosted and how often is it updated?
2) For customers in the EU, do you transfer API request data outside the EU as part of hosted API usage, and what safeguards apply?

If you can give a one-line host/update cadence and a brief sentence on transfers (e.g., SCCs + encryption + regional routing where offered), we can quickly include it in our procurement evaluation.

- Maya

Maya Singh
Procurement Lead
Acme Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA snippets + subprocessor phrasing for public site

Maya / Evelyn —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Below is a concise set of publishable lines that address Acme's questions and are suitable for the hosted API product card and DPA FAQ. We can link the live subprocessor registry from the FAQ paragraph.

Product card (one-line):
"We process API request data to generate model outputs; we do not use customer API request data to train our public models, and access is controlled by audit logs and contractual safeguards."

FAQ snippet (2–3 sentences):
"We engage a limited set of subprocessors (cloud infrastructure and security providers) to operate the hosted API. We publish a live subprocessor registry (updated monthly) and restrict subprocessors' access to only the data necessary to run the service. For cross-border transfers, we rely on standard contractual safeguards (e.g., SCCs), encryption in transit and at rest, and regional routing options for customers who require EU-only processing."

Notes:
- "Updated monthly" is conservative but aligns with our current process; happy to change to "quarterly" if ops prefers.
- If Acme requires contractual wording about SCCs or a tailored DPA clause, we should route that through Legal (Rishi) for signature.

If that reads OK, Evelyn — please share back to Acme and ask if they want the DPA redline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Counsel
Redwood Inference
